articles.title: Keytruda Biosimilars Face Market Barriers and Formulary Adoption Hurdles
articles.summary: Upcoming Keytruda biosimilars face significant commercialization hurdles, including complex patent litigation and entrenched brand loyalty, which threaten projected savings for self-funded employers. For PBMs and plan sponsors, overcoming these adoption barriers is critical to unlocking specialty drug cost reductions for high-spend oncology therapies.
articles.source_line: Source: BioPharma Dive; Mon, 02 Nov 2026 14:41:59 GMT

articles.title: DOL PBM Disclosure Rule Aimed at Lowering Employer Health Plan Drug Costs
articles.summary: The Department of Labor has introduced a new PBM disclosure rule designed to increase transparency and reduce prescription drug costs for employer-sponsored health plans. This regulation directly impacts self-funded employers by shedding light on hidden PBM fees and administrative pricing structures. Plan sponsors will gain critical data needed to better evaluate pharmacy benefit contracts and manage plan spending.
articles.source_line: Source: New Jersey Business & Industry Association; Mon, 02 Nov 2026 19:07:01 GMT

articles.title: New DOL Rule Grants Employers Greater Visibility into PBM Fees
articles.summary: A new Department of Labor rule requires pharmacy benefit managers to provide self-funded employers with detailed disclosures regarding fee structures and pricing transparency. This regulation strengthens plan sponsors' fiduciary oversight by enabling them to audit costs and evaluate true PBM compensation. The mandate will likely accelerate contract renegotiations and demand for fully transparent pass-through models across self-funded health plans.
articles.source_line: Source: Insurance Business; Mon, 02 Nov 2026 15:55:04 GMT

articles.title: DOL Finalizes ERISA PBM Fee Disclosure Rules for 2026
articles.summary: The Department of Labor has finalized new PBM fee disclosure requirements under ERISA, increasing compliance obligations for self-funded plan sponsors. Plan sponsors must now carefully review their PBM contracts and fee structures to ensure transparency and fiduciary alignment. This regulatory shift directly impacts how self-funded employers evaluate their PBM arrangements and manage administrative costs.
articles.source_line: Source: Crowell & Moring LLP; Mon, 02 Nov 2026 23:18:51 GMT

articles.title: DOL Final Rule Expands PBM Transparency for Self-Insured Health Plans
articles.summary: The Department of Labor has issued a final rule increasing transparency requirements for Pharmacy Benefit Managers operating within self-insured health plans. This regulatory shift directly impacts how self-funded employers monitor PBM contracts, fee structures, and drug pricing practices. Plan sponsors will gain enhanced oversight capabilities to audit and evaluate the true cost of their pharmacy benefits.
articles.source_line: Source: Consumer Financial Services Law Monitor; Mon, 02 Nov 2026 20:22:36 GMT

articles.title: Rising Job-Based Health Plan Costs Compound Pressure on Employers
articles.summary: Employer-sponsored health insurance costs continue to climb steadily with no immediate relief in sight, driven largely by escalating medical and pharmacy benefit expenditures. This trend increases the urgency for self-funded employers to adopt aggressive cost-containment strategies, benefit design optimization, and transparent pharmacy management to protect their bottom lines.
articles.source_line: Source: Buffalo News; Mon, 02 Nov 2026 17:00:00 GMT

articles.title: Starbucks Evaluates GLP-1 Coverage Cuts Amid Rising Employer Cost Pressures
articles.summary: Starbucks is reportedly considering cutting employee health plan coverage for GLP-1 weight-loss drugs while simultaneously adapting its product offerings to cater to consumers using these medications. This highlights the escalating tension self-funded employers face between managing runaway specialty drug costs and accommodating workforce health trends. For self-funded plans and PBMs, this signals growing employer pushback against unsustainable GLP-1 spending and a shift toward stricter benefit design exclusions.
articles.source_line: Source: The Seattle Times; Mon, 02 Nov 2026 15:10:39 GMT

articles.title: Congressional Action Needed on Safe Step Act to Curb Payer Utilization Management
articles.summary: An opinion piece calls on Congress to pass the Safe Step Act, arguing that current insurance and PBM step therapy protocols undermine patient care. For self-funded employers and PBMs, federal restrictions on step therapy could impact benefit design flexibility and utilization management strategies used to control specialty drug costs.
articles.source_line: Source: Washington Reporter; Mon, 02 Nov 2026 19:25:37 GMT

articles.title: Novo Nordisk and Andel Launch Employer Workaround for GLP-1 Coverage
articles.summary: As self-funded employers increasingly restrict GLP-1 coverage due to runaway costs, drugmaker Novo Nordisk and partner Andel are rolling out alternative benefit designs and workarounds to maintain employee access. This development directly impacts employer cost-containment strategies and challenges traditional PBM formulary management for obesity medications.
articles.source_line: Source: The American Journal of Managed Care; Mon, 02 Nov 2026 07:12:42 GMT
articles.source_name: The American Journal of Managed Care

articles.title: Employers Bear the Cost of 340B Drug Price Spreads
articles.summary: A new report reveals that self-funded employers are shouldering the heavy financial burden of 340B drug spread pricing within their health plans. This hidden cost inflation directly impacts employer drug spend and heightens the demand for greater PBM transparency and reform.
articles.source_line: Source: HR Dive; Mon, 02 Nov 2026 15:47:14 GMT

articles.title: Employers Beginning to Drop GLP-1 Coverage Due to High Costs
articles.summary: Growing numbers of companies are rolling back or eliminating coverage for expensive GLP-1 weight-loss drugs as plan costs surge. This trend highlights the difficult balancing act self-funded employers face between offering competitive benefits and managing runaway pharmacy spend. PBMs must guide plan sponsors on alternative coverage strategies, prior authorization, and lifestyle management programs to control these liabilities.
